cohort: Women undergoing cesarean section at a tertiary obstetric unit between December 2014 and November 2018
finding: Routine intraoperative cell salvage during cesarean section may reduce the need for blood transfusion, with a small risk of fetal cell alloimmunization in subsequent pregnancies (1 in 436).
mod_finding: This study focused on intraoperative cell salvage during cesarean sections and its impact on subsequent pregnancies, not on comparing different modes of delivery.
